# Deep time - age of the Earth, strata and fossils (`deep_time_geology`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/physics.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Physics, optics & astronomy (`physics`)
- Deps: helped by radioactivity, natural_causes
- Core idea: The Earth is immensely old (about 4.5 thousand million years) and its surface records processes still at work: rain and rivers wear the land down, the debris settles in layers on sea floors, hardens to rock and is later raised and folded into mountains. In an undisturbed sequence of sedimentary layers the lower ones are older. Fossils are the remains of real creatures; sea shells on mountains show that the rock was once sea floor. Each group of layers has its own fossils, in the same order everywhere, so rocks can be matched across countries and coal or ore seams followed. Many kinds of animals have died out. Since 1907 the decay of uranium to lead in minerals has given ages in years.
- Pitfalls:
  - Giving the age with no way to show it; before radioactivity only rates of deposition and erosion could be argued, and they gave anything from thousands to hundreds of millions of years
  - Saying all strata were laid down by one flood
  - Putting people together with dinosaurs, or mixing up millions and thousands of millions
  - Ignoring that the claim contradicts the accepted chronology of about 6000 years in Christian and Islamic lands (but not Indian cosmology)
- History: greece: c. 500 BC – Xenophanes takes inland shells and fish imprints as proof of a former sea; islamic: c. 1027 – Ibn Sina, Book of Healing: mountains formed by uplift and erosion over long ages; china: 1088 – Shen Kuo infers shifted coastlines and climate change from fossil shells and petrified bamboo; india: Hindu and Jain cosmology reckons with cycles of thousands of millions of years (not based on rocks); europe: c. 1508 Leonardo's notes on fossils; 1669 Steno's principles of strata; 1788 Hutton; 1796 Cuvier establishes extinction; 1815 William Smith's geological map; 1830–1833 Lyell; 1862 Kelvin's too-short 20–400 million years; 1913 Holmes's radiometric timescale; americas: 1907 Boltwood's first uranium-lead ages; 1956 Patterson: 4.55 thousand million years
- Read:
  - James Hutton, Theory of the Earth, Transactions of the Royal Society of Edinburgh 1 (1788)
  - Martin J. S. Rudwick, Earth's Deep History: How It Was Discovered and Why It Matters (2014)
